title: Stable model locking and resolution: tag/semver/commit pin semantics for SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Teams using the Redwood API/SDK need a single, predictable way to pin model versions so production workloads get deterministic inference behavior while retaining ergonomics for model updates. Current behavior is inconsistent across SDKs: some clients accept tag names, others accept semver ranges, and resolution fallbacks are underspecified. This ticket defines canonical pin semantics and SDK behaviour for three primary pin types: tag (stable alias), semver (range or exact), and commit-hash (immutable reference).

Goals:
- Define deterministic resolution order for host and private deployments.
- Make pin usage explicit in SDK request surface so telemetry and billing reflect resolved model versions.
- Ensure immutable pins (commit-hash) guarantee reproducible inference across time.
- Provide ergonomics for safe auto-rollforward policies (optional) based on semver ranges and tag tracking.

Summary of proposed semantics:
1) Pin kinds accepted by API/SDK: 
   - commit:<sha>  => exact immutable model artifact. Resolution is direct, no fallback.
   - tag:<name>    => logical alias managed by model catalog (e.g., tag:stable, tag:experimental). Resolves to the catalog's current artifact. Resolution updates when the tag is moved.
   - semver:<expr> => semver expression (e.g., 1.3.0, ^1.2.0, >=1.2 <2.0). Resolved to the highest compatible release in the model catalog.
   - unpinned / model_family:<name> => server chooses a default per customer tier/policy. This remains supported but discouraged for production.

2) Resolution order and fallbacks: 
   - commit:<sha> -> resolve and enforce. If artifact missing: return 404 with clear error code (MODEL_PIN_NOT_FOUND). No implicit fallback.
   - semver:<expr> -> resolve to best match. If no match, optional fallback to tag:stable if enabled by customer policy. Otherwise return 422 with REASON=NO_COMPATIBLE_VERSION.
   - tag:<name> -> resolve to referenced artifact. If tag points to an unpublished or deleted artifact, return 409 with TAG_INVALID. Optional customer-configurable fallback to latest-compatible semver is allowed.

3) Runtime behaviour and SDK surface: 
   - SDKs will accept a single header/query/body field "model_pin" and an optional "pin_fallback_policy" with values ["none","tag->semver","semver->tag","allow-unpinned"]. Default for hosted is "none".
   - On resolution, the server returns "resolved_model_ref" in response metadata containing the resolved kind (commit|release|tag), resolved_version, and performance_profile_id. SDKs will surface this via response.resolvedModelRef.
   - Telemetry: every request must annotate the resolved_model_ref in usage logs and cost breakdown so unit economics map to resolved artifact.

4) Performance profile publishing: 
   - Every model artifact has an associated published performance profile id. The resolution response must include which performance_profile_id was used for scheduling decisions. This is critical for capacity planning and cost attribution.

Trade-offs & reasoning:
- Immutable commit pins offer reproducibility at the cost of ergonomics; we keep them strict with no fallback to avoid surprise regressions.
- Semver ranges are developer-friendly but risk accidental pulls of newer models with behaviour changes. We require explicit customer opt-in for automatic rollforwards (pin_fallback_policy) and recommend canarying.
- Tags are simple for product teams (e.g., "stable") but can hide drift; therefore tags must be visible in Console and have an audit trail in model catalog.

Edge cases and error semantics:
- When resolution takes longer than X ms (configurable), server should return a 202 with polling link and resolution status for long-running catalog lookups.
- If resolved_model_ref changes between request start and execution (race during tag move), server uses the artifact locked at scheduling time and returns a warning header "X-Model-Pin-Race" when observed.

Backward compatibility: 
- If a caller supplies legacy field "model" we treat it as unpinned family with a deprecation warning in response headers. SDKs will log deprecation to client telemetry.

Acceptance criteria:
- API accepts model_pin values matching grammar commit:<hex>|tag:<name>|semver:<expr>.
- SDKs for JS, Python, and Go implement the model_pin param and surface resolvedModelRef in response objects.
- Server emits resolved_model_ref with performance_profile_id in logs and response metadata for all pinned requests.
- Console shows a mapping of tag -> artifact history and indicates which customers used tag pins in the last 30 days.

Implementation notes:
- Model catalog service must expose lookup endpoints for semver queries with deterministic tie-breaking (prefer GA/stable releases, otherwise highest patch).
- Add a small cache layer in runtime for resolved pins with TTL=5m for tags and semver to reduce catalog load; commit pins bypass cache. Catalog changes must invalidate TTLs immediately for affected tags.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (runtime-2.4): Add backend resolution API and response metadata. Add logging. Roll out to 10% of hosted traffic for testing.
- Phase 2: SDK updates + Console UI to show resolved refs. Enable tag audit trail.
- Phase 3: Opt-in customer pin fallback policies and public docs.

- Catalog API PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/487
- Initial runtime change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1293
- Console workboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ModelPinConsoleWork
acceptance_criteria: API accepts model_pin and validates grammar for commit:tag:semver
Server includes resolved_model_ref and performance_profile_id in response metadata for pinned requests
JS/Python/Go SDKs surface resolvedModelRef and deprecation warnings for legacy model field
Console exposes tag history and customer usage for tags
Catalog supports deterministic semver resolution with documented tie-breaker
test_plan: Unit tests for grammar parsing and server validation (commit/tag/semver)
Integration test that asserts commit:<sha> is immutable across time and returns MODEL_PIN_NOT_FOUND for unknown sha
Property tests for semver resolution with mock catalog responses (cover edge ranges and tie-breakers)
E2E canary: route 1% traffic to new resolver and compare resolved_model_ref and perf profile mapping against control
Load test: TTL cache reduces catalog QPS for tag resolution by at least 75% under synthetic traffic
